body:
**Clause:** 2017 §25.7.3 pp.764-765 and §25.7 p.761 / 2023 §25.7.3.
**Normative (the standard example):** a modport with `export Read` and a module `memMod(interface a)` that defines `task a.Read; ... endtask`; "If the subroutines are defined in a module using a hierarchical name, they shall also be declared as extern in the interface or as export in a modport."
**Probes:** tests/1800_audit/c25/t_export.sv, and the reducers reduce_export_generic.sv and reduce_export_typed.sv (the interface-port types generic and named).
**Observed** (identical under -g2017 and -g2023): the task definition `task a.Read(...)` fails to compile: "a already declared in this scope, previously declared as a net", followed by a syntax error. The interface-port type is not the cause (both reducers fail the same way). Importing tasks defined inside the interface works (t_import.sv prints the expected MRD, MWR and SRD lines, including a parameterized interface).
**Expected:** the module defines the exported task, and a call through the master modport runs it (EREAD 4, then EDATA 5).

Provenance: build b9441baf (descendant of origin/main 8c95b5cc). Probes on branch m7-1800-audit-c08, tests/1800_audit/c25/. Logs: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c25d-20261020/.
title: [IEEE 1800] §25.7.3 — a module cannot define a task exported through a modport (task a.Read)

body:
**Clause:** 2017 §25.7.4 pp.765-766 / 2023 §25.7.4.
**Normative:** "So that these can still export their read and write tasks, the tasks shall be declared in the interface using the extern forkjoin keywords." The standard example declares `extern forkjoin task countSlaves();` in an interface and exports it from several module instances through a modport.
**Probes:** tests/1800_audit/c25/t_forkjoin.sv and the one-line reducer reduce_extern_forkjoin.sv.
**Observed** (identical under -g2017 and -g2023): both fail at the first `extern forkjoin` declaration with a syntax error.
**Expected:** the declaration is accepted and one call runs every exported definition: two instances of the same modport type each increment a counter, so the call leaves the counter at 2 (SLAVES 2).

Provenance: build b9441baf (descendant of origin/main 8c95b5cc). Probes on branch m7-1800-audit-c08, tests/1800_audit/c25/. Logs: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c25d-20261020/.
title: [IEEE 1800] §25.7.4 — extern forkjoin task declarations in an interface are a syntax error
